shorts_extract.hook: In 1996 at Virginia, psychologists played loud brass marching music while asking tired volunteers to fall asleep as fast as possible — and trying harder backfired!
shorts_extract.core_experiment: In 2018 at Baylor University, 57 young adults wired to overnight polysomnography wrote for 5 minutes before bed: completed-task writers took 25.1 minutes to sleep, while to-do list writers fell asleep in 15.8 minutes.
shorts_extract.twist: Offloading specific future tasks onto physical paper lets your hippocampus and prefrontal cortex stand down like a night watchman clocking out.
